noData.body: “No data” means no value was reported. INFORM leaves it out of the category average. It is never treated as zero, and zero is a real, low score. The exceptions are the workbook’s own: coastal erosion scores 0 for every unit because its reference range maps every value to 0, and livelihoods is 0 in most units (see Limitations on the Methodology page).
noData.tooltip: No value reported, so it is left out of the average (not counted as zero).

services.drrSource: Source: the Prime Minister's Office (Disaster Management Department) lists of June 2026 and its communication of 10 October 2026, the published launches and trainings of 2023-2026, and the district and regional disaster-management committees through the Data portal, each record approved by the next level. The five arrangements scored are the plan, the assessment, the trained team, the centre and the training; an arrangement not recorded counts as not in place.
services.committeeLead: The three criteria PMO-DMD and the committees assess; the share met is the committee-functioning indicator of the Governance group. A criterion not assessed is not scored.

steps.indicators: Each indicator group is scored from 0 to 10, where higher always means more risk.
steps.categories: A category is the average of its indicator groups; groups without data are skipped, never counted as zero.
steps.dimensions: A dimension combines its categories with INFORM’s scaled geometric mean, rounded to one decimal.
steps.risk: INFORM Risk is the cube root of Hazard & Exposure × Vulnerability × Lack of Coping Capacity.

level.council: Councils share their INFORM source unit’s vulnerability and coping data because household surveys have no council breakdown.
level.region: Regions are rebuilt from their councils’ indicator averages rather than by averaging council risk scores: the INFORM combination is not linear, so the two would give different results.
level.source: INFORM source units: the district-level backbone of the Tanzania INFORM workbook, used here as the reference level.
level.national: The national value ({{value}}) is the INFORM aggregate of all councils, computed as for regions. The Tanzania workbook publishes no national score, and the INFORM Global country score uses other indicators and is not comparable.

notes.title: Read with care
notes.core: The Core is never changed by this layer; approved institutional values take effect in the Core.
notes.intensity: These sub-indicators measure hazard intensity on each territory (rainfall, temperature, slope, wind, seismicity), not the people exposed, as INFORM’s own hazard indicators do.
notes.ranges: Each member is standardised once against a fixed reference range set from the span of the {{councils}} council values (relative scaling, as the workbook does); the weights are proposed, not yet calibrated.
notes.district: Members marked “District figure” were computed on the 2022 district and copied to its councils.
notes.coverage: {{filled}} of {{total}} sub-indicators have data (release {{release}}); the others are documented as withheld or unavailable on the Methodology page.
